prompt: The sides of a rectangle are measured as $5.0 \pm 0.1\ \text{cm}$ and $2.0 \pm 0.1\ \text{cm}$. What is the percentage uncertainty in the area?
What are the SI base units of power?

A student measures the period $T$ of a simple pendulum for different lengths $L$ and plots $T^2$ against $L$. The best-fit line has gradient $4.10\ \text{s}^2\,\text{m}^{-1}$; the maximum and minimum gradient lines have gradients $4.25$ and $3.95\ \text{s}^2\,\text{m}^{-1}$.

**(a)** Explain why $T^2$ is plotted against $L$. **[1]**

**(b)** Determine $g$ and its absolute uncertainty. **[3]**

**(c)** The line has a small positive intercept on the $T^2$ axis. Suggest one cause. **[1]**
markscheme:
**(a)** $T^2 = \tfrac{4\pi^2}{g}L$, so the graph should be a straight line through the origin ✓

**(b)** $g = \tfrac{4\pi^2}{4.10} = 9.63\ \text{m s}^{-2}$ ✓; gradient uncertainty $= \tfrac{4.25 - 3.95}{2} = 0.15$, i.e. 3.7% ✓; $\Delta g \approx 0.04\times9.63 \approx 0.4$, so $g = 9.6 \pm 0.4\ \text{m s}^{-2}$ ✓

**(c)** $L$ measured to the top of the bob rather than its centre (a systematic error in length) ✓
